17These things I command you, that ye love one another. - John 15:17 (KJV)

 Jesus made it so very clear, that we were to love one another, and again He commands us to love one another. He commanded us to love one another as He has loved us (John 15:12). Jesus said that the greatest of all the commandments was to love God with all our hearts, and love our neighbor as ourselves (Mark 12:30-31). Jesus made it clear that all the law was fulfilled by these two commandments (Matthew 22:40). What an amazing thing it was for Jesus to take all the rules and regulations of the Old Testament Law, and sum them up in two commands of love – Wow!

 This illustrates that all the things that were commanded for people to do under the law were just pictures of what love would have us do, if we would just love one another. So many Christians still don’t understand that under the New Testament Covenant that we have with God, we are not told we have to do works to be right with God, but we just have to love Him and others. The wonderful thing is that if you truly love God, and others, you will do all those things that were commanded under the law, but it will be done out of love, and not out of obligation. This takes all the pressure off of the Christian, if you understand this, and it does away with condemnation (Romans 8:1), which is the greatest tool that the devil uses against us. Praise God for making us a loving machine, instead of a doing machine.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com

TIL what causes phantom traffic jams. The physics of traffic jams.

If this was more widely known and impatient drivers behind you were eliminated all it would take is a few drivers implemting some of the tactics mentioned to greatly reduce traffic congestion in built up areas.
I wonder how self-driving cars will react to traffic jams like this. I know that if there were only self-driving cars there would be no or at least not nearly as many traffic jams.

There is a good chapter on this in Philip Ball's 'Critical Mass: How One Thing Leads to Another' where he talks about how a standing wave in traffic patterns can be created and remain in place for a long time after. The conclusion seemed to be that with self-driving cars, as long as they can transmit information between each other, could break as a whole to avoid cascading differences in reaction.

Civil Engineers that do highway design are well versed in this phenomenon. Part of their job is highway design that at least mitigates the effects of "phantom" jams. Its funny how people driving like assholes to get somewhere faster are the ones that end up slowing everything down.

The zipper merge isn't really as perfect as everyone seems to think. These illustartions assume everyone knows what everyone else is doing at all times and knows what their future behavior will be as well...obviously this isn't realistic. It's a good idea in theory and works sometimes but it simply isn't going to work 100% of the time because even if everyone is aware of the tactic they aren't aware of other drivers' current and future thoughts and behaviors.

Leaving a larger gap between you and the car in front of you mitigates most problems. When cars are driving too close to each other and the one in front brakes it causes a wave of braking; this leads to jams. Leaving a large cushion between you and the car in front allows you to NOT necessarily have to use your brakes if they do and simply coast until the leading car gets off the brake and this will not cause a wave of braking because you did not have to use yours.

Little bit of column A, little bit of column B. Zipper merges aren't a "one size fits all" solution.

God I hope Voat doesn't become a zipper merge circlejerk...
